nodes.text:
Here's a thread on EVERYTHING you need to know about hMPV.
Human metapneumovirus (hMPV) is a common respiratory virus that causes an upper respiratory infection (similar to a normal cold).

nodes.author: audiooo0_v0rt3x
nodes.text:
It is a seasonal disease that occurs in the winter and early spring, similar to RSV and the flu.
*Children, people with weakened immune systems and the elderly are most susceptible to developing complications from the infection.* 
It is spread by close contact with an infected person or contact with a contaminated area.

nodes.author: audiooo0_v0rt3x
nodes.text: It usually causes SYMPTOMS similar to the common cold that last roughly 2-5 days and go away on their own. Most children who get infected are age 5 or younger. A small number of children (5-16%) infected will develop a lower respiratory tract infection such as PNEUMONIA.

nodes.author: audiooo0_v0rt3x
nodes.text:
People at a higher risk-> 
It is most common in young children and the elderly in whom it is more likely to develop into bronchiolitis, bronchitis or pneumonia.
Though a history of asthma, COPD, emphysema or any other lung disease does not make someone more likely to contract the illness, once they have it, these lung diseases can make symptoms more severe. This is also true for people with weakened immune systems, including patients undergoing chemotherapy or post organ transplant.

nodes.author: audiooo0_v0rt3x
nodes.text:
Symptoms include
1)Cough
2)Runny nose or nasal congestion
3)Sore throat
4)Fever

nodes.author: audiooo0_v0rt3x
nodes.text: In more severe cases, patients may experience wheezing, difficulty breathing and asthma flare-ups. Secondary lower respiratory infections may occur such as bronchiolitis, bronchitis or pneumonia, requiring additional medical care.

nodes.author: audiooo0_v0rt3x
nodes.text: The best way to protect from infection is to avoid touching people who are infected. If you think you are infected, keep others safe by covering your mouth when you cough, avoiding touching and sharing possibly infected items and washing your hands.

nodes.author: audiooo0_v0rt3x
nodes.text:
People with chronic lung diseases such as COPD, asthma and pulmonary fibrosis should always take precautions to protect from infections such as hMPV, influenza and other contagious diseases.
PREVENTION IS BETTER THAN CURE.
